newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yen fall too rapid in light of trade friction-MITI.
newsitem.headline: Yen fall too rapid in light of trade friction-MITI.

text.p: Japan's Minister of Trade and Industry Shinji Sato said on Friday that the current fall in the yen was too rapid and added that he hoped for stability in currencies in light of Japan's trade friction with the United States.

"(The current yen fall) is too rapid. Excessive volatility is problematic. I would hope for more stable currency moves, in light of the fact that there is trade friction between Japan and other countries, mainly the United States," Sato told reporters.

He also added: "There seems to be concern that the weaker yen will increase exports, but there is a need for Japan to change fundamentally to a domestic demand-led economy and not to adjust fine points here and there."
Sato was speaking at his regular press conference after the cabinet meeting.
